# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Smit_2019_tobramycin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Smit_2019_tobramycin"))$description`
* Article: [Pharm Res 2019;36(8):112](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-019-2651-2)
  (open access, PMC6542779)
* Correction: [Pharm Res 2020;37(2):27](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-020-2756-7)
  (PMC7050552), which reprints Table 2 with corrected units and formula.

# Population

Smit 2019 enrolled 20 morbidly obese adults (BMI > 40 kg/m^2, or > 35
kg/m^2 with comorbidities) scheduled for laparoscopic gastric sleeve or
bypass surgery and 8 non-obese healthy volunteers (BMI 18-25 kg/m^2) at
St. Antonius Hospital, Nieuwegein, The Netherlands (Table I). Obese
patients had a median total body weight of 137.8 kg (range 103-194),
median BMI 41.9 kg/m^2 and median age 43.0 years; non-obese volunteers had
a median weight of 66.3 kg (range 57-91), BMI 22.2 kg/m^2 and age 22.5
years. 15 of the 28 participants were female. Everyone had normal renal
function (eGFR >= 60 mL/min); the de-indexed MDRD eGFR had medians of 127.5
mL/min (range 77-171) in the obese and 102.6 mL/min (91-120) in the
non-obese group.

Obese patients received a single 5 mg/kg dose of tobramycin based on
lean body weight (Janmahasatian), and non-obese volunteers 5 mg/kg based
on total body weight, both as 0.5-h IV infusions. Ten plasma samples per
participant were taken over 24 h (280 in total, 23 below the 0.3 mg/L
LLOQ and handled with the M3 method).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Smit_2019_tobramycin")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to the source.
All values come from the final-model column of Table 2 as reprinted in the
2020 correction, which supersedes the original Table II.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL at MDRD 115 mL/min) | log(6.33) L/h | Corrected Table 2, CL_MDRD115 |
| `e_crcl_cl` (Z) | 0.0099 per mL/min | Corrected Table 2, Z; Fig. 5 nomogram equation |
| `lvc` (Vc at 70 kg) | log(10.6) L | Corrected Table 2, Vc70kg |
| `lq` | log(6.69) L/h | Corrected Table 2, Q |
| `lvp` | log(4.34) L | Corrected Table 2, Vp |
| `etalcl` | 0.014297 | Corrected Table 2, IIV CL 12.0% -> log(1 + 0.12^2) |
| `etalvc` | 0.060142 | Corrected Table 2, IIV Vc 24.9% -> log(1 + 0.249^2) |
| `propSd` | 0.116 | Corrected Table 2, proportional error |
| `addSd` | 0.346 mg/L | Corrected Table 2, additive error |
| `cl = CL115 * (1 + Z * (CRCL - 115))` | n/a | Corrected Table 2 row header; Methods Eq. 4 |
| `vc = Vc70kg * (WT / 70)` | n/a | Corrected Table 2 row header; Methods Eq. 3 with X = 1 |
| Two-compartment, first-order elimination from central | n/a | Results, Pharmacokinetic Analysis |
| IIV exponential on CL and Vc | n/a | Methods Eq. 1; Results |
| Combined additive and proportional error | n/a | Methods Eq. 2; Results |

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Smit_2019_tobramycin")
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
```

# Covariate: de-indexed MDRD

The clearance covariate is the 4-variable MDRD eGFR multiplied by the
individual's body surface area / 1.73, so it is in mL/min, **not** mL/min/1.73
m^2. Supplying the usual BSA-normalized eGFR would understate clearance in
obese patients, whose BSA is well above 1.73 m^2. The helper below follows
the equations in the paper's supplement (MDRD with creatinine in umol/L and
the Du Bois BSA).

```{r mdrd-helper}
mdrd_deindexed <- function(creat_umol, age, female, black, wt, height_cm) {
  mdrd <- 186.3 * (creat_umol / 88.4)^-1.154 * age^-0.203 *
    ifelse(female == 1, 0.742, 1) * ifelse(black == 1, 1.210, 1)
  bsa <- 0.007184 * wt^0.425 * height_cm^0.725
  mdrd * bsa / 1.73
}
# A 140 kg, 175 cm, 40-year-old woman with creatinine 70 umol/L
mdrd_deindexed(70, 40, 1, 0, 140, 175)
```

# Replication of the study design

A virtual cohort of 200 obese and 200 non-obese participants reproduces the
study's dosing and sampling. Weight, height and renal function were not
reported per participant, so they are drawn to match the Table I medians
and ranges (out-of-range draws are rejected and redrawn, never clamped).
Obese doses use the Janmahasatian lean body weight, which needs sex and BMI,
so height is drawn from sex-specific normal distributions and BMI is
computed.

```{r cohort-helpers}
draw_in_range <- function(n, draw, lo, hi) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- draw(2 * n)
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lo & x <= hi])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

lbw_janmahasatian <- function(wt, bmi, female) {
  ifelse(
    female == 1,
    9270 * wt / (8780 + 244 * bmi),
    9270 * wt / (6680 + 216 * bmi)
  )
}

make_study_cohort <- function(n, obese, id_offset) {
  female <- rbinom(n, 1, if (obese) 11 / 20 else 4 / 8)
  if (obese) {
    # Reject-and-redraw on both weight and BMI ranges of Table I.
    wt <- numeric(n)
    ht <- numeric(n)
    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      repeat {
        w <- exp(rnorm(1, log(137.8), 0.15))
        h <- rnorm(1, if (female[i] == 1) 168 else 181, 7)
        b <- w / (h / 100)^2
        if (w >= 103 && w <= 194 && b >= 36 && b <= 53) break
      }
      wt[i] <- w
      ht[i] <- h
    }
    bmi <- wt / (ht / 100)^2
    crcl <- draw_in_range(n, function(m) rnorm(m, 127.5, 22), 77, 171)
    dose <- 5 * lbw_janmahasatian(wt, bmi, female)
  } else {
    wt <- draw_in_range(n, function(m) exp(rnorm(m, log(66.3), 0.12)), 57, 91)
    crcl <- draw_in_range(n, function(m) rnorm(m, 102.6, 7), 91, 120)
    dose <- 5 * wt
  }
  tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    group = if (obese) "Morbidly obese" else "Non-obese",
    WT = wt,
    CRCL = crcl,
    amt = dose
  )
}
```

```{r study-cohort}
set.seed(2019)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
n_arm <- 200
subj_study <- bind_rows(
  make_study_cohort(n_arm, obese = TRUE, id_offset = 0L),
  make_study_cohort(n_arm, obese = FALSE, id_offset = n_arm)
)

subj_study |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    "Median WT (kg)" = median(WT),
    "Median de-indexed MDRD (mL/min)" = median(CRCL),
    "Median dose (mg)" = median(amt),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename("Group" = group) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Virtual study cohort; compare Table I (dose medians 340 and 320 mg).")

# Paper sampling: 5 min after the end of the 0.5-h infusion, then 1, 1.5, 2,
# 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 6, 12 and 24 h after the start of infusion.
study_times <- c(0, 0.5 + 5 / 60, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 6, 12, 24)
fine_times <- sort(unique(c(study_times, seq(0, 24, by = 0.25))))

study_events <- bind_rows(
  subj_study |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "central", rate = amt / 0.5),
  subj_study |>
    select(id, group, WT, CRCL) |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = fine_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", rate = 0)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
```

Each dose row carries an explicit infusion rate of `amt / 0.5` mg/h, so the
dose runs over 0.5 h.

```{r study-sim}
sim_study <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = study_events,
  keep = c("group", "WT", "CRCL")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

## Concentration-time profiles (cf. Figure 1)

```{r figure-1}
sim_study |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(group, time) |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(sim),
    sd = sd(sim),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, mean, colour = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(mean - sd, 0.05), ymax = mean + sd), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.3, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of infusion (h)",
    y = "Tobramycin concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    title = "Simulated mean +/- SD tobramycin concentrations",
    caption = "Compare with Figure 1 of Smit 2019. Dotted line: 0.3 mg/L LLOQ."
  )
```

## PKNCA against the observed AUC24 and Cmax

The paper computed AUC24 per participant with the trapezoidal rule on the
observed samples, and defined Cmax as the concentration 1 h after the start
of infusion (Methods, Pharmacokinetic Analysis). To compare like with like,
PKNCA is run here on the same ten sampling times with the linear trapezoidal
rule, which overestimates the AUC of an exponential decline across the
6-12-24 h gaps just as the paper's calculation did.

```{r pknca-study}
conc_study <- sim_study |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), time %in% study_times) |>
  select(id, group, time, Cc)
stopifnot(all(table(conc_study$id) == length(study_times)))

dose_study <- subj_study |>
  mutate(time = 0, duration = 0.5) |>
  select(id, group, time, amt, duration)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_study, Cc ~ time | group + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  dose_study, amt ~ time | group + id,
  route = "intravascular", duration = "duration"
)
intervals_study <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)
nca_study <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  conc_obj, dose_obj,
  intervals = intervals_study,
  options = list(auc.method = "linear")
))

c1h <- conc_study |>
  filter(time == 1) |>
  transmute(id, group, PPTESTCD = "c1h", PPORRES = Cc)

sim_ind <- as.data.frame(nca_study) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, group, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  bind_rows(c1h)

# The paper reports arithmetic means, so the simulation is summarised the
# same way before the comparison.
sim_mean <- sim_ind |>
  group_by(group, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(PPORRES = mean(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")

reference <- data.frame(
  group = c("Morbidly obese", "Non-obese"),
  auclast = c(56.1, 70.0),
  c1h = c(11.8, 18.3)
)

cmp_study <- ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_mean, reference,
  by = "group",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L", c1h = "mg/L")
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp_study,
  caption = paste(
    "Mean AUC0-24 (linear trapezoidal, study sampling times) and",
    "concentration 1 h after start of infusion (the paper's Cmax definition),",
    "simulated vs. Smit 2019 Results."
  )
)
```

```{r pknca-study-check}
pct <- sim_mean |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(reference, by = "group", suffix = c("_sim", "_ref")) |>
  mutate(
    auc_pct = 100 * (auclast_sim - auclast_ref) / auclast_ref,
    c1h_pct = 100 * (c1h_sim - c1h_ref) / c1h_ref
  )
# The simulated means sit a few percent below the observed means (see
# Assumptions and deviations); a transcription error in CL, Z, Vc or a dose
# unit would move them by far more than 25%.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(pct$auc_pct) < 25),
  all(abs(pct$c1h_pct) < 25)
)
```

## AUC0-inf self-consistency

For a single IV dose AUC0-inf must equal the dose divided by each subject's
individual clearance. Both sides use the same drawn parameters, so the only
differences are trapezoidal error and the lambda-z extrapolation on the
dense grid.

```{r pknca-aucinf}
conc_dense <- sim_study |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, group, time, Cc)
nca_dense <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_dense, Cc ~ time | group + id),
  dose_obj,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))
chk <- as.data.frame(nca_dense) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  select(id, group, aucinf = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(sim_study |> group_by(id) |> summarise(cl = first(cl)), by = "id") |>
  left_join(subj_study |> select(id, amt), by = "id") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (aucinf - amt / cl) / (amt / cl))

chk |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    "Median AUC0-inf (mg*h/L)" = median(aucinf),
    "Median % diff vs dose/CL" = median(pct_diff),
    "90th pct |% diff|" = quantile(abs(pct_diff), 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename("Group" = group) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  abs(median(chk$pct_diff)) < 2,
  quantile(abs(chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 5
)
```

# Dosing simulations (Figure 4, Table S1)

The paper's Monte Carlo simulation used 9,993 individuals with weights
uniformly distributed between 60 and 190 kg, and de-indexed MDRD drawn from
normal distributions with mean 137 mL/min (SD 34) for obese and 112 mL/min
(SD 23) for non-obese individuals (Methods, Model-Based Simulations). Those
up to 100 kg are the non-obese group. Here 200 individuals per weight group
are simulated for each regimen, each as a single 0.5-h infusion, and AUC24
is computed by PKNCA on a dense grid (linear-up/log-down).

* **Nomogram**: Dose (mg) = 75 x 6.33 x (1 + 0.0099 x (MDRD - 115))
  (Figure 5 caption).
* **5 mg/kg TBW**.
* **5 mg/kg scaled TBW**: 5 x 70 x (TBW/70)^0.42 mg (Figure S2C caption).

The fourth regimen of Table S1, 5 mg/kg adjusted body weight, needs height
and sex for the ideal body weight, and the paper does not give their
simulated distributions, so it is not reproduced.

```{r mc-cohort}
set.seed(75)
mc_subj <- bind_rows(
  tibble(group = "Non-obese", WT = runif(n_arm, 60, 100), CRCL = rnorm(n_arm, 112, 23)),
  tibble(group = "Obese", WT = runif(n_arm, 100, 190), CRCL = rnorm(n_arm, 137, 34))
)
stopifnot(min(mc_subj$CRCL) > 20)

regimens <- list(
  "Nomogram (MDRD-based)" = function(d) 75 * 6.33 * (1 + 0.0099 * (d$CRCL - 115)),
  "5 mg/kg TBW" = function(d) 5 * d$WT,
  "5 mg/kg TBW^0.42" = function(d) 5 * 70 * (d$WT / 70)^0.42
)
mc_subj_all <- bind_rows(lapply(names(regimens), function(r) {
  mc_subj |> mutate(regimen = r, amt = regimens[[r]](mc_subj))
})) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())

mc_times <- c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.1), seq(2.5, 24, by = 0.5))
mc_events <- bind_rows(
  mc_subj_all |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "central", rate = amt / 0.5),
  mc_subj_all |>
    select(id, group, regimen, WT, CRCL) |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = mc_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", rate = 0)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
```

```{r mc-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(75)
sim_mc <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = mc_events,
  keep = c("group", "regimen", "WT", "CRCL")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r mc-nca}
conc_mc <- sim_mc |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, group, regimen, time, Cc)
dose_mc <- mc_subj_all |>
  mutate(time = 0, duration = 0.5) |>
  select(id, group, regimen, time, amt, duration)
nca_mc <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_mc, Cc ~ time | regimen + group + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_mc, amt ~ time | regimen + group + id,
    route = "intravascular", duration = "duration"
  ),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE),
  options = list(auc.method = "lin up/log down")
))
auc_mc <- as.data.frame(nca_mc) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, group, regimen, AUC24 = PPORRES)

table_s1 <- tribble(
  ~regimen, ~group, ~paper_median, ~paper_lo, ~paper_hi, ~paper_within,
  "Nomogram (MDRD-based)", "Non-obese", 75.0, 57.4, 93.5, 93.4,
  "Nomogram (MDRD-based)", "Obese", 74.2, 56.9, 92.8, 93.6,
  "5 mg/kg TBW", "Non-obese", 65.0, 23.3, 116.8, 48.0,
  "5 mg/kg TBW", "Obese", 94.6, 22.2, 184.1, 40.4,
  "5 mg/kg TBW^0.42", "Non-obese", 60.9, 24.1, 105.7, 44.6,
  "5 mg/kg TBW^0.42", "Obese", 61.6, 18.8, 115.5, 41.8
)

mc_summary <- auc_mc |>
  group_by(regimen, group) |>
  summarise(
    sim_median = median(AUC24),
    sim_lo = quantile(AUC24, 0.025),
    sim_hi = quantile(AUC24, 0.975),
    sim_within = 100 * mean(AUC24 >= 0.8 * 75 & AUC24 <= 1.25 * 75),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(table_s1, by = c("regimen", "group")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff_median = 100 * (sim_median - paper_median) / paper_median)

mc_summary |>
  select(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "Group" = group,
    "Median (paper)" = paper_median, "Median (sim)" = sim_median,
    "% diff median" = pct_diff_median,
    "2.5th pct (paper)" = paper_lo, "2.5th pct (sim)" = sim_lo,
    "97.5th pct (paper)" = paper_hi, "97.5th pct (sim)" = sim_hi,
    "% within 60-93.75 (paper)" = paper_within, "% within (sim)" = sim_within
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "AUC24 (mg*h/L) by regimen and weight group, simulated vs. Table S1.")
```

The medians are the structural check: they depend only on the typical
clearance, the MDRD slope and the dose rule. The percentiles and the
fraction within 80-125% of target also depend on which subjects land in
the tails and are shown for comparison only.

```{r mc-check}
stopifnot(all(abs(mc_summary$pct_diff_median) < 10))
```

```{r figure-4}
auc_mc |>
  filter(regimen != "5 mg/kg TBW^0.42") |>
  left_join(mc_subj_all |> select(id, WT, CRCL), by = "id") |>
  filter(
    (group == "Non-obese" & regimen == "5 mg/kg TBW") |
      (group == "Obese" & regimen == "Nomogram (MDRD-based)")
  ) |>
  mutate(wt_band = cut(WT, breaks = seq(60, 190, by = 10), include.lowest = TRUE)) |>
  ggplot(aes(wt_band, AUC24)) +
  geom_jitter(aes(colour = CRCL), width = 0.2, size = 0.8) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA, coef = 0) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 75, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.8, 1.25) * 75, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = "darkblue", high = "darkred") +
  labs(
    x = "Total body weight (kg)",
    y = "AUC24 (mg*h/L)",
    colour = "De-indexed\nMDRD (mL/min)",
    title = "5 mg/kg TBW below 100 kg, MDRD nomogram above 100 kg",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Smit 2019 (200 simulated individuals per weight group)."
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Correction applied.** The original Table II printed CL and Q in L/min,
  Vp as 4.35 L and the CL formula with an unbalanced parenthesis. The 2020
  correction reprints the table with CL and Q in L/h, Vp 4.34 L and
  `CL = CL_MDRD115 * (1 + Z * (MDRD - 115))`; the model uses the corrected
  values. The Figure 5 nomogram, `Dose = AUC24 x 6.33 x (1 + 0.0099 x
  (MDRD - 115))`, confirms CL in L/h.
* **Central volume is linear in weight.** Table 2 writes `Vc = Vc70kg *
  (TBW/70)` with no exponent, and Table III lists 8 parameters for the base
  model with TBW on Vc (4 structural, 2 IIV, 2 residual), so no exponent was
  estimated.
* **Residual error entries are standard deviations.** The additive error is
  printed in mg/L, so both residual entries are read as SDs, entering as
  Eq. 2 `Y = Cpred + Cpred * eps1 + eps2`.
* **IIV as CV%.** The IIV percentages are converted with
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`, which matches the exponential model of Eq. 1.
* **No IIV on Q or Vp**, as reported.
* **BLQ handling.** The M3 method used in estimation does not affect
  simulation.
* **Virtual study cohort.** Individual weights, heights, sex and MDRD values
  are not published; they are drawn to the Table I medians and ranges, with
  sex-specific heights (168 cm female, 181 cm male, SD 7 cm) chosen by the
  maintainers to produce the Table I BMI range. The simulated median doses
  are about 320 mg (obese) and 340 mg (non-obese) against Table I medians
  of 340 and 320 mg: the virtual obese lean body weights come out slightly
  below the Table I median of 69.3 kg, and the non-obese weights slightly
  above 66.3 kg.
* **Observed AUC24 and Cmax.** The simulated means fall a few percent
  below the observed means of Smit 2019 Results (56.1 and 70.0 mg*h/L; 11.8
  and 18.3 mg/L), with the larger gap in the non-obese group. This matches
  the paper's own statement that all covariate models "seemed to slightly
  underpredict tobramycin concentrations below 10 mg/l in the non-obese
  individuals". The parameters are not tuned to close this gap.
* **Lower tail of Table S1.** The simulated medians, upper percentiles and
  within-target fractions match Table S1, as do both percentiles for the
  nomogram. The lower 2.5th percentiles that Table S1 gives for the two
  weight-based regimens (18.8-24.1 mg*h/L) are not reproduced (simulated
  about 36-54). They cannot be reached with the stated MDRD distributions:
  an AUC24 of 22 mg*h/L for a 100-kg patient on 5 mg/kg TBW needs a clearance
  of about 23 L/h, i.e. a de-indexed MDRD near 375 mL/min, about seven SDs
  above the stated obese mean of 137 mL/min. The paper does not give
  enough detail of its simulation to explain the difference.
* **Monte Carlo cohort.** The paper drew MDRD from untruncated normal
  distributions; the same is done here, with an assertion that no simulated
  MDRD falls low enough to make clearance non-positive. The 5 mg/kg
  adjusted-body-weight regimen of Table S1 is not reproduced (height and sex
  distributions not reported).
